repo.description: ## Summary The `ImageElement` component in `packages/gazzodown` renders user-controlled `src` values directly into `` and `` attributes without protocol sanitization. Unlike the analogous `LinkSpan` component - which uses `sanitizeUrl` to block `javascript:`, `data:`, and `vbscript:` protocols - `ImageElement` passes the raw URL through unchanged. An authenticated user can post a markdown image with a `javascript:` URL that, if clicked on an older browser, would execute arbitrary JavaScript in the viewer's session. ## Severity **Medium** (CVSS 3.1: 4.4) `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N` - **Attack Vector:** Network - any authenticated user can post markdown messages - **Attack Complexity:** High - exploitation requires the victim to use a browser that does not block `javascript:` navigation with `target='_blank'` (all modern browsers do block this) - **Privileges Required:** Low - any authenticated user can post messages - **User Interaction:** Required - victim must click the rendered image link - **Scope:** Changed - JavaScript executes in the victim's browser session, crossing the application boundary - **Confidentiality Impact:** Low - could access session tokens or page content if executed - **Integrity Impact:** Low - could perform actions as the victim if executed - **Availability Impact:** None ## Affected Component - `packages/gazzodown/src/elements/ImageElement.tsx` - `ImageElement` (line 52) ## CWE - **CWE-79**: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') ## Description ### Missing sanitizeUrl on ImageElement The `ImageElement` component renders the `src` prop directly into the `href` attribute of an `` tag without any protocol sanitization: ```tsx // packages/gazzodown/src/elements/ImageElement.tsx:48-56 const ImageElement = ({ src, alt }: ImageElementProps): ReactElement => { const plainAlt = useMemo(() => flattenMarkup(alt), [alt]); return ( ); }; ``` ### Inconsistent defense with LinkSpan The `LinkSpan` component handles the analogous case for markdown links and correctly applies `sanitizeUrl`: ```tsx // packages/gazzodown/src/elements/LinkSpan.tsx:18-20 const LinkSpan = ({ href, label }: LinkSpanProps): ReactElement => { // Should sanitize 'href' if any of the insecure prefixes are present - see DSK-34 on Jira const sanitizedHref = sanitizeUrl(href); ``` The `sanitizeUrl` function (at `packages/gazzodown/src/elements/sanitizeUrl.ts`) specifically blocks dangerous protocols: ```typescript const dangerousProtocols = ['javascript:', 'data:', 'vbscript:']; return dangerousProtocols.includes(url.protocol.toLowerCase()) ? '#' : url.href; ``` Both `ImageElement` and `LinkSpan` receive their URL from the same parser AST via `InlineElements.tsx`. The IMAGE case at line 55 passes `block.value.src.value` directly, while the LINK case at line 46 routes through `LinkSpan` which sanitizes. ### Execution chain 1. An authenticated user posts a message containing `![test](javascript:alert(document.domain))` 2. The message parser (`packages/message-parser`) parses this as an IMAGE node. The grammar's `URLScheme` rule (`$([A-Za-z0-9+-] |1..32| ":")`) accepts `javascript:` as a valid scheme. The `MarkdownLinkFilePath` alternative matches the full URL. 3. Server-side validation in `sendMessage.ts` checks `javascript:` only on **attachment URL fields** (thumb_url, image_url, etc.), NOT on URLs in the message body text. 4. `InlineElements.tsx:55` renders `` 5. `ImageElement.tsx:52` outputs `` - **no sanitization applied** 6. In a legacy browser, clicking the image would execute JavaScript in the victim's session. In modern browsers, `target='_blank'` prevents execution. ## Proof of Concept ``` # Post in any Rocket.Chat room as an authenticated user: ![click me](javascript:alert(document.domain)) # The rendered image will be a broken image wrapped in an tag. # The href attribute contains the raw javascript: URL. # Clicking the link in a browser that does not block javascript: with target='_blank' # would execute the payload. # In modern browsers (Chrome 90+, Firefox 87+, Safari 14+), clicking opens about:blank instead. # The vulnerability is confirmed by DOM inspection: the unsanitized href is present in the rendered HTML. ``` ## Impact - Unsanitized `javascript:` and `data:` URLs are rendered into the DOM via `` on every message view - On legacy browsers lacking `target='_blank'` javascript: blocking, clicking the image executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's session context - Stored XSS - the payload persists in the message and is rendered for every viewer of the channel - Could lead to session hijacking, credential theft, or actions performed as the victim (on vulnerable browsers) - Defense-in-depth gap - the codebase relies solely on browser behavior rather than applying its own available sanitization ## Recommended Remediation ### Option 1: Apply sanitizeUrl to ImageElement (preferred) ```tsx // packages/gazzodown/src/elements/ImageElement.tsx import { sanitizeUrl } from './sanitizeUrl'; const ImageElement = ({ src, alt }: ImageElementProps): ReactElement => { const plainAlt = useMemo(() => flattenMarkup(alt), [alt]); const safeSrc = sanitizeUrl(src); return ( ); }; ``` This is the minimal, consistent fix - applying the same defense already used by `LinkSpan`. The `sanitizeUrl` function is in the same directory, already tested, and blocks `javascript:`, `data:`, and `vbscript:` protocols. ### Option 2: Add server-side URL protocol validation in the message parser Add protocol validation at the parser level in `packages/message-parser/src/grammar.pegjs` to reject `javascript:`, `data:`, and `vbscript:` schemes in Image URLs. This would prevent dangerous URLs from entering the AST at all, protecting all downstream consumers. However, this is a larger change and Option 1 should be applied regardless for defense in depth. ## Credit This vulnerability was discovered and reported by [bugbunny.ai](https://bugbunny.ai).
repo.summary: Missing URL protocol sanitization in ImageElement allows javascript: URLs in markdown images
